name: session-wiki
title: A wiki compiled from past sessions

conditions.corpus: the second shipyard corpus: 209 sessions, 139 questions, each asked in the sessions' own words and paraphrased
conditions.pages: compiled by Claude Sonnet from the 167 earliest sessions, one agent per stream; every claim cites a quote that ctx wiki save found word for word in its session. Small: 25 pages. Large: 183 pages
conditions.held back: the 42 latest sessions, which hold the answers to 38 questions; no page could cite them
conditions.control: the same pages with their citations reassigned at random, to separate reaching the right session from reaching more sessions
conditions.answers: ctx as installed, with and without the large wiki; both phrasings; 3 runs each; graded blind in one pass per phrasing

summary: Whether pages compiled from session history help agents answer questions about past work, the consolidation idea in Anthropic's article on agent memory. Retrieval was gated first, with no agent runs; answers were then compared over 1,668 runs.

metrics.label: Retrieval, own words: no pages, large wiki
Answers, paraphrased: no wiki, large wiki
metrics.note: better on 38, worse on 27, p = 0.22; bar +8

metrics.label: Answers, paraphrased, the 101 questions the pages cover

bar: retrieval of paraphrased questions rises to 35 of 139; then answers gain 8 of 139 with no more wrong answers, or match with 20% fewer tokens
meaning: Small wikis do nothing; a large one lifts retrieval clearly above its control and answers a little, exactly on the questions its pages cover. The gain, about 4% on paraphrased questions, does not clear the bars, so ctx does not compile wikis from sessions.
